cells.tense: The clearing is happening now, here, and it is being done with the pen.
cells.act: do the plain version first, before the plans
cells.ask: Whatever you're clearing out today, take the plainest version of it and start there — ahead of the planning, ahead of the tidier arrangement.
cells.core:
You can tell the difference between a thing that's actually finished and a thing you'd just like to be finished. When a shape built on a false premise comes down, it comes down clean, and you don't scramble to rebuild it the same way. You let it land, then look at the ground it left.

The small daily work is what makes this real. You practise the plain version, not the polished one, and the practice keeps you upright while the rest comes apart. Practising doesn't pretend nothing is ending; it gives the ending somewhere to land. Whatever gets built from here gets built on what you actually did, not on what you meant to.
cells.sheetLine: You're clearing what can't hold, and the practice holds you.

cells.tense: The clearing will be finished before the thing has finished being built.
cells.act: keep the ritual and give it room to change
cells.ask: Keep one practice that was handed to you, as it is, and let a single part of it bend to fit what you know now.
cells.core:
Lately everything is coming down fast, and some of it was still carrying weight. It reads as liberation from outside; standing in the middle of it, the walls go before anyone has said a proper goodbye. Nothing gets to stand long enough to be tested, so nothing gets to be trusted, and you're on to the next collapse before this dust settles.

What other hands have carried forward gets you through. Keep one of the practices you were given, and let exactly one part of it bend to fit what you know now. You don't invent a container from scratch, and you don't freeze it either. Something handed on can stay alive and still hold. That's what makes the next ending survivable.
cells.sheetLine: You're knocking it all down before any of it has stood.

cells.tense: The structure stopped holding a while back, and it is still being propped up.
cells.act: build the smallest structure that holds it
cells.ask: Give the mess that's been sitting there a rule, a place, and a time — the least that keeps it off your arms.
cells.core:
Something in your life already gave way, and you're still keeping it upright. The fixing happens quietly now, in the gaps, and it takes more of each day than the thing ever did when it worked. You keep saying the next step is the one that matters.

A frame moves you where a shove won't. Put a rule, a time and a flat surface around the mess, and the edges will carry what your arms have been carrying. You don't need to feel ready to give something a shape. Once the shape exists, the part that already gave way stops pretending it hasn't. One small structure, kept, is the whole move.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding up something that has already let go.

cells.tense: The clearing is already underway, and it is being done without knowing.
cells.act: move toward the thing you want, one step, today
cells.ask: Take one step today toward what you actually want — not what's convenient, the direction your own momentum is leaning.
cells.core:
Something is being cleared near you and you haven't named it yet. By the time it's obvious, the ground will have shifted and you'll describe the change as something that happened to you rather than something you did. Signs come in small pieces — a habit you've quietly dropped, a door you've stopped standing in front of — and they get filed under a busy week.

What you want is already leaning you somewhere, and following it for a single step is enough to make the direction visible. You don't have to name the whole structure that's coming down. Move in the direction your own energy is going, and let your hand do what it was reaching for anyway. Naming it comes second. The step comes first.
cells.sheetLine: It's already coming down, and you haven't said so yet.
